issue.testName: a realtime effect header remains reachable after dragging toward the window edge

originalFullRun.observation: The screenshot confirms that the title and close control are above the viewport. The next horizontal-reachability assertion was not reached.

isolatedRerun.command: PULSE_SERVER=unix:/mnt/wslg/PulseServer PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=4364 npx playwright test tests/browser/audio-editor-dialog-navigation-regressions.spec.js --config=/tmp/perf200-browser-recheck.config.mjs --project=firefox --workers=1 --grep='a realtime effect header remains reachable after dragging toward the window edge' --trace=on --output=/tmp/perf200-dialog-navigation-recheck-results
isolatedRerun.config: Import the worktree playwright.config.mjs and export its settings with an absolute tests/browser testDir and webServer: []; use the already running frozen product sites.
isolatedRerun.traceObservation: EffectParameterEditor lazy chunk request began at monotonic 8765.660 ms; the header bounding-box action began at 8806.387 ms and resolved at 9154.138 ms; mouse-down followed at 9275.771 ms. The body was present before dragging in this successful run.

method: Create a temporary Playwright spec importing test/expect and the existing bootEditor, chooseCommandAction, openEffectsForTrack and addRackEffect helpers by absolute worktree paths. Use the real Firefox project at its default 1280 by 720 viewport.

Before boot, install page.route("**/EffectParameterEditor-*.js", async route => { await released; await route.continue(); }), where released is a manually resolved Promise. Record the requested URL. Release the Promise in finally as well to avoid leaving a blocked route.

Boot /embed/en/, invoke Generate > Tone with default settings, generate, open the first track effects rack, and add Reverb through its menu. Wait for the Reverb dialog and intercepted request, and verify [data-effect-parameters] has count zero.

Read bounding boxes for the dialog and .dialog-header. Move to the header center, mouse.down(), mouse.move(1, 1, { steps: 5 }), and mouse.up(). Poll the header bounding box until its y equals 8; capture the empty-body edge screenshot.

Resolve released so the original chunk continues unmodified. Wait until [data-effect-parameters] is visible, then read the dialog/header bounding boxes and capture the loaded-body screenshot. Attach those observations as JSON; assert loaded.header.y equals -21.5 only in this temporary diagnostic.

Use a temporary config importing the actual worktree playwright.config.mjs, overriding only testDir to the temporary spec directory, testMatch to **/*.spec.mjs, and webServer to []. Run one Firefox worker with tracing and a separate output directory; keep the full-suite process and its artifacts untouched.
deterministicDiagnostic.confirmedMechanism: LazyEffectParameterEditor uses Suspense fallback=null. The backdrop centers the dialog with CSS grid. AudioEditorDialogShell captures header bounds at mousedown and retains the same transform after the body mounts. Growing from 160 to 219 px shifts the centered origin upward by 29.5 px, moving a previously clamped header from y=8 to y=-21.5.

changedCallerReview.finding: The round-three change memoizes workspace panel availability/grouping/presentation. The effects-window dialog and its positioning are owned by the unchanged effects overlay, dialog shell and CSS; no causal defect in this new caller was identified.

classification.confirmed: A pre-existing bounds defect can be triggered by mounting the real lazy effect body after an edge drag; the controlled reproduction matches the original -21.5 px failure exactly. Its relevant production and test sources are byte-identical to the merged baseline.
classification.unresolved: The original full-run diagnostics have no trace, so the actual lazy-load/resize timing in that original run cannot be directly established. The isolated pass does not erase or convert the original full-run failure into a full-suite pass.

covered: Fixed header bounds at all viewport edges
A subsequent drag after a previously translated header
existingTestCoverage.gap: No panel-size/lazy-body change during or after dragging is covered.

proposedFutureCorrection.scope: Re-clamp a draggable dialog when its panel size changes, and synchronize active drag geometry so later mouse moves cannot restore stale bounds.
redTests: Hold the real lazy effect chunk, drag the empty dialog to the edge and release the pointer; load the body and retain the original header y>=0 and horizontal-reachability assertions.
Load the body during an active drag, then continue moving and release; the header must remain reachable.
proposedFutureCorrection.performanceCountEffect: None. A separate dialog-layout correctness fix must not expand or replace the frozen 100 performance changes.

repositoryChanges: Only this intentional diagnostic JSON is added. No production implementation, existing test, assertion, generated artifact, dependency or runtime inventory was altered.

additionalIssues.testName: Repeat last effect retains its Amplify gain after a new dialog is canceled

originalFullRun.observation: The workflow reached the final exported-audio peak check. The received peak equals the unamplified quiet fixture after centered stereo routing. The upper-bound assertion was not reached.

isolatedRerun.config: Import actual worktree playwright.config.mjs, retain its real product origin/project settings, override testDir with absolute tests/browser and webServer: [], and reuse the frozen preview sites.

method: Create a temporary spec using the real browser fixture and existing helpers. Import mono 330 Hz WAV fixtures of 0.8 seconds, amplitude 0.35 and 0.175, named repeat-loud.wav and repeat-quiet.wav. Select the loud clip header.

After import and before opening Amplify, temporarily wrap OfflineAudioContext.prototype.startRendering in that page only. Call the original method unchanged; for only the first call, return nativeRendering.then(async buffer => { await held; return buffer; }), where held is a manually resolved Promise. Record call/native-completion/release performance.now timestamps. Later calls return their native rendering Promises normally. Preserve and restore the original prototype method in finally, and resolve held there as well.

Open Effect > Volume and compression > Amplify, wait for the real Apply effect dialog and first startRendering call. Verify Apply to selection is enabled while the first preparation result is held. Record the visible input values; both Amplification and New peak amplitude show 0.

Click Apply to selection without releasing held. Wait for the dialog to hide and record that a second native render was started; this apply completes using the stale explicit gainDb 0. Restore the native method and resolve held only after the first apply completes.

Mute the loud track, select the quiet clip, reopen Amplify, close its dialog, and choose Effect > Repeat last effect. Wait for the normal enabled Export audio control and export through the existing fresh-URL exportSamples helper. Compute the decoded PCM peak. In the temporary diagnostic only, assert it equals 0.12373518943786621 exactly.

Use the real frozen product sites, a temporary config importing the actual project config with webServer: [] and a temporary testDir, one Firefox worker, tracing, screenshots and an independent output directory. Do not alter the original spec/assertions or interrupt the full browser run.
deterministicDiagnostic.confirmedMechanism: openSelectionEffect starts asynchronous automatic-gain preparation without waiting before opening the dialog. SelectionEffectsDialog enables Apply and submits local selectionParams. Applying while the scan is pending supplies gainDb 0 as an explicit touched value, so resolveInteractiveAudacityParams preserves it; lastAudacityEffect and Repeat then retain that gain. The controlled preparation delay reproduces the original final peak without changing rendered PCM.

sharedDependencyReview.finding: The mono fixture does not enter the direct stereo dry-PCM path, so graph/PDC preparation changes are reachable in preparation and export. It has no VCA, solo or suspended effect; those changed registrars/resolvers take neutral paths. Edge-width and PDC indexes remain reachable. No concrete regression was found in those changes, but immediate-source parity is not treated as causal exclusion of every shared dependency.
sharedDependencyReview.exportSynchronization: The existing exportSamples helper captures the previous download URL and polls until a new URL appears before decoding. The original test waits for an enabled Apply button, not completed automatic-gain preparation; it later waits for enabled Export audio, not a measured Repeat PCM result.

classification.confirmed: A pending automatic-gain scan plus an early Apply reproduces the exact exported peak. Its workspace/dialog/effect-control/execution/rendering glue is byte-identical to the merged baseline, establishing that this unchanged control flow admits the race.
classification.unresolved: The original full-run failure has no trace and its preparation timing is not observable. This is not a whole baseline-build reproduction, and reachable shared graph/PDC changes can affect scheduling. The original failure remains unexplained with an isolated pass and a matching controlled race; it is not marked causally excluded or converted into a passing full-suite receipt.

covered: Automatic gain from complete target PCM
An explicit gain edit while asynchronous preparation runs wins
existingTestCoverage.gap: The mounted dialog Apply action enabled during pending preparation and submitting untouched stale local gain is not covered.

proposedFutureCorrection.scope: Coordinate automatic-gain preparation with dialog Apply readiness, and preserve the distinction between untouched automatic defaults and explicit gain edits.
redTests: Hold automatic-gain preparation in the mounted dialog; Apply must not commit stale untouched local gain.
Retain explicit user gain edits during preparation and the saved Repeat gain after reopening/canceling another dialog.
proposedFutureCorrection.performanceCountEffect: None. Any separate synchronization correction is outside the frozen 100 performance improvements.

baselineIsolation.priorAssertions: Timeline audio deletion, the card No audio label and video visibility all passed.
baselineIsolation.method: Create a clean detached worktree at the merged baseline, build both browser products without source or test edits, serve its Soundscaper and Framescaper bundles on 4366/4367, and run the unchanged exact WebKit test with one worker and trace:on. The test boots Framescaper, so no current-product preview server is reused. Stop only these two diagnostic servers and remove only the detached baseline worktree after retaining logs, screenshots and traces.

sourceReview.labelObservation: The No audio label uses the same itemClips audio-membership condition as the muted prop and passed in both baseline and current runs.
sourceReview.newMemoScope: Grouping/source joins depend on owning published collections. The memoized media timing resolves only duration, start, end and rate; the muted expression remains direct.
sourceReview.backendObservation: The video branch publishes a frozen preview containing clip/bin IDs, state, kind and mediaUrl; it does not set a DOM mute property. Repository searches found no native muted=false assignment in editor/Framescaper. Other native decoding helpers set their separate video elements muted=true.
